title: I reported 93 of 93 packs blocked by four checks that cannot block anything

first_order.what_broke: I told the founder that house_quote, house_style, human_register and repetition were blocking all 93 finished packs off the shelf, and framed it as a generator-versus-linter spec mismatch. All four are deliberately un-armed and emit zero errors. I had counted warnings as failures.
first_order.receipt: pack_linter.py:2137 sets ok = not any(p['severity'] == 'error' for p in problems). config.yaml:1636 lint_repetition_block false, config.yaml:1708 human_register_block false, house_style.py:344,348,352,357 hardcoded _warn. Real blockers across 74 packs: shelf_copy 42, placeholders 21, title 16, citation_urls 6, sections 3.

cause_chain: ops/automations/stranded_packs.py collected every problem code from the lint receipts without reading the severity field.
The lint receipt carries severity per problem, so the data was right there and the reader dropped it.
A check that fails 100 percent of a population should have been read as a measurement fault, not a population fault. I reported the number instead of questioning it.
CLASS: an aggregate that ignores severity turns advisory output into a false blocker list, and it reads as a confident finding.

second_order.sweep_command: rg -n "problems|findings" ops/automations/ scripts/ --type py | rg -v severity
second_order.note: docs/doc_lint_baseline.json is the same shape at a different layer and is tracked separately as INC-2026-08-18-doc-rot-ratchet.

third_order.mechanism: stranded_packs.py now filters on severity == 'error' before counting. The stronger guard is still missing: nothing fails when a new aggregator reads a problems list without reading severity.

grade.signature: an aggregate over lint problems with no severity filter
